issues.body:
After the flag and gate were dropped, ROLE_LABELS has no production consumer — both readers are inside `_self_test` (664, 839). Its content is, by the new `catalog == the pinned live role labels` assertion, definitionally identical to `{lb for lb in REAL if lb.startswith('role:')}`, which is already declared 790 lines lower.

This is fine as-is: the assertion makes the duplication safe (drift goes red), and having a short prefix-free name at the top of the file makes the `derived_roles` check readable. Recording it only so a future reader does not mistake ROLE_LABELS for a live catalog that something writes labels from — nothing does.
issues.fix_hint: No change required. If you want to shed the duplicate literal entirely, `derived_roles <= {lb[5:] for lb in REAL if lb.startswith('role:')}` expresses the same invariant against the already-pinned set and lets both ROLE_LABELS and the catalog-equality check go away. Either shape is defensible; keeping the named catalog plus the equality assertion is the more legible of the two.
issues.title: ROLE_LABELS is now a test-only constant that duplicates REAL's role subset

issues.body:
The diff removes `[OPUS-4.8]` from the scripts/triage.py and .github/workflows/triage-issue.yml headers, which is correct under the model-agnostic provenance rule. But `grep -c 'OPUS-5|FABLE-5|OPUS-4|SONNET'` still returns 9 in scripts/triage.py — e.g. the `[FABLE-5]` markers at 118/123 and the `[OPUS-5]` markers at 133/244. So the file is left half-swept.

Entirely cosmetic and explicitly out of this PR's scope if the sweep is staged; not a reason to withhold approval.
issues.fix_hint: Either finish the sweep in a follow-up (strip the remaining inline `[MODEL-X]` markers; the maintainer-decision dates and PR/issue numbers in those comments carry the provenance that actually matters), or add one line to the PR description saying the header removal is the first slice of a staged sweep so the inconsistency is not read as an oversight.
issues.title: Model-marker sweep is partial — 9 inline markers remain after the two header removals

verdict.summary:
Round 3 resolves both round-2 majors and both minors. Verified against the checkout, not just the diff.

MAJOR #1 (dead `--role-labels` flag + orphaned color/description payload) is GONE. `grep -rn 'role-labels|ROLE_LABELS' . --exclude-dir=.git` now returns exactly three hits, all in scripts/triage.py: the definition (49) and two self-test consumers (664, 839). No argparse flag, no printer, no tuple payload. ROLE_LABELS is a plain `frozenset({docs,impl,ci,research,site})` — the membership set it was always used as. Nothing claims label reconciliation any more, so the false promise is gone too.

MAJOR #2 (silent explicit-role demotion) is GONE. scripts/triage.py:230-232 is back to `explicit = ...; if len(explicit) == 1: return explicit[0]` with no static catalog gate. The #582 warn-and-preserve contract at 285-295 is once again the sole authority, driven by the LIVE label set (`known = repo_label_set(repo)`), and it keeps the incumbent role plus a loud warning rather than returning None.

MINOR #3 fixed: the check is renamed to `trust role replacement plans no churn when the target is already present`, which is exactly what `(False, False)` asserts. Traced by hand: `area:worker` hits SEC_KEYWORDS -> role impl, target already present, so add/remove are both empty after the `add - labels` / `remove & labels` narrowing. Name and body now agree.

MINOR #4 fixed twice over. `derived_roles` now folds in `set(AREA_ROLE_DEFAULT.values())`, matching the producer set the neighbouring REAL check at 858 already used, and it derives the UI/INFRA roles by calling `_role()` rather than hard-coding {site, ci} — slightly stronger than its neighbour. More importantly the drift check now exists: `catalog == the pinned live role labels` binds `{role:<k> for k in ROLE_LABELS}` to `{lb for lb in REAL if lb.startswith('role:')}`, so the two hand-maintained literals can no longer disagree silently.
